questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to win an argument with your friends
Why politicians disagree with each other so often
If society is more divided and how to be open
How modern dating apps match people
questions.why: Beth asks whether we're becoming more divided and how we can be more accepting of others' opinions.

questions.q: What does Neil say about his friends' opinions?
options: They're similar to his, partly why they're friends
They are very different from his own views
He never discusses his opinions with friends
He often argues with his friends about politics
questions.why: Neil says he probably has quite similar opinions, 'and that's, kind of, why we're friends'.

questions.q: According to Beth, how might social media make us less accepting?
options: It shows us far too many different opinions
It makes people spend less time with family
It only shows us news from other countries
Its algorithms show what we already agree with
questions.why: She says algorithms tend to show us what we already like and agree with.

questions.q: What does Professor Paul Dolan suggest people could do on social media?
options: Stop using it completely
Wait five minutes before sending a post
Only post happy messages
Block people who disagree with them
questions.why: He says people could have a five-minute delay before sending.

questions.q: What does Paul say about calming down when you're very angry?
options: It is impossible to calm down quickly when angry
It usually takes about an hour to feel better
Anger never really goes away once it starts
It takes 15 minutes, but starts within seconds
questions.why: He says it takes 15 minutes for the amygdala to calm down, but it starts within a few seconds.

questions.q: What does Paul suggest about anger?
options: It isn't always bad, as it can motivate us
It should always be avoided
It helps us make the best decisions
It is only a problem online
questions.why: He says always being calm isn't necessarily good: 'Anger can be motivational.'

questions.q: What did the dating experiment find?
options: Most people only cared about their partner's height
People want open minds in others, not themselves
People prefer partners with different political views
Open-minded people find partners faster
questions.why: Researchers concluded people want a tolerant partner but don't want to be very open-minded themselves.

questions.q: What does Paul think is the best way to become more tolerant?
options: Reading more news online from different sources
Only talking to people who agree with you
Going offline and meeting different people
Avoiding any talk about politics with friends
questions.why: He says to get offline and meet people; the more you're around different people, the more tolerant you become.
